definition: In cognition, mental representation refers to the internal structuring of information that supports action and learning. In this source, it is discussed in motor learning as the way movement patterns and strategies are mentally organized and related to performance.

reasons: The packet text does not explicitly define “mental representation” as an “internal structuring of information” that “supports action and learning”; it only mentions “mental representation structures” in relation to motor learning/performance.

The packet provides support only for a motor-learning framing (movement patterns/strategies via “cognitive primitives” representing specific movement patterns and strategies), not for the broader cognition-wide description used in the definition.

The phrase “internal structuring of information that supports action and learning” is broader than the packet supports; the packet only says the study examines mental representation structures and introduces “cognitive primitives” as units representing movement patterns and strategies.

“Mental representation” is not defined in the packet as the way movement patterns and strategies are “mentally organized”; that wording goes beyond the source’s description of their relation to performance.
